newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI in southern Africa iron ore deal - papers.
newsitem.headline: JCI in southern Africa iron ore deal - papers.

text.p: South Africa's JCI Ltd and international partners have begun a feasibility study into a three billion rand iron ore project in Mozambique and Zimbabwe, newspaper reports and industry sources said.
JCI was not available for comment on Thursday.
The reports said that the planned project would utilise gas from Mozambique's Temane gas field to feed an iron ore reduction plant to be built on the Mozambique/Zimbabwe border.
The plant would produce hot bricketted iron (HBI) for export from Mozambique's Beira port to the Pacific Rim for use as a feedstock in mini steel mills, the reports said.

JCI's partners in the project include U.S.-based Arco Chemical Co, the United Arab Emirates's Zarara Petroleum Resources, the Mozambican and Zimbabwean governments, Mozambique's state energy company and Buchwa Iron Mining (Bimco), Business Report newspaper said on Wednesday.
Zarara held an exclusive study agreement with Arco and JCI relating to the use of the Temane gas for the iron ore reduction project, industry sources said.
Arco will appraise the feasibility of the development and operation of the Temane gas field as a dedicated source and the transportation of the gas to the plant.
According to the reports, JCI will determine the feasibility of mining the iron ore deposits in Zimbabwe and developing and operating the planned iron ore reduction plant.
Canada's Leopardus Resources Ltd, which has signed a letter of intent to acquire Zarara's rights to the Temane permit area, will act as liaison with Mozambican authorities.
Newspaper reports quoted JCI as saying said the planned project was still in the beginning stages but a final decision to go ahead could be taken in a year's time.
Business Report quoted JCI Beira project leader Hugh Brown as saying the project represented the first commercial use of combined gas and iron resources in the southern African region.
Brown told the newspaper the project would include a 450 km gas pipeline and gasfield development at a cost of $180 million.

The reduction plant would be erected at a cost of $280 million, the iron ore mine and benefication plant would cost around $100 million and the construction of infrastructure would cost about $100 million.
